name: Enterprise V2 — multi-tenant portals, roles, consultant licensing, talent marketing
summary: Multi-tenant enterprise portals on the one shared deployment: each organization gets its own domain and branded login, configurable multi-role workspaces, consultant licenses priced as a base plus feature add-ons, and the talent-marketing pipeline (consultants submit; marketers prepare; HR and Finance record only). DESIGN COMPLETE: 46 design docs, 154 stories, every part of the requirements covered. BUILD: Phase 1 foundation under way (X1.1-X1.5 done: flags, tenancy schema, tenant resolution, branded-host web routing, tenant-bound sessions).

epics.name: Phase 0 — Audit, debate, foundation design, plan
epics.goal: The design set under docs/enterprise-v2 that every later phase builds from; 23 ADRs; escalations for the user.

epics.name: Phase 1 — Enterprise tenant foundation
epics.goal: Hostname → tenant resolution the client can never influence, tenant-bound sessions, roles as data, the invitation framework, and the negative-test gate — before any protected feature.

epics.name: Phase 2 — Branded login and dashboard shell
epics.goal: Runtime branding, one branded login, one enterprise shell with permission-driven workspaces, Org Admin lands on the Org Admin Dashboard, basic profile from the avatar menu, the Kiwiply character used compactly.

epics.name: Phase 3 — Custom domains
epics.goal: careers.acme.com: registration, ownership verification, on-demand certificates through the shared edge, activation, primary/redirect, suspension, removal, monitoring.

epics.name: Phase 4 — Roles, employees, departments, teams, assignments
epics.goal: Configurable role templates with a ceiling rule, employee lifecycle with bulk actions and audit, departments/teams, auditable consultant–marketer assignments.

epics.name: Phase 5 — Subscription foundation
epics.goal: Catalog (shared with personal plans), feature definitions and dependencies, base license + add-ons, pricing engine with contracts, entitlement evaluation, usage ledger, personal-subscription regression suite.

epics.name: Phase 6 — Billing and license UI, Stripe org billing
epics.goal: Subscription Overview, Consultant Licenses, Configure License with backend quotes, Billing & Invoices, Feature Usage, Platform Pricing Admin; one Stripe subscription per org; reconciliation.

epics.name: Phase 7 — Consultant and resume management
epics.goal: Consultant directory and profile overlay, org-managed resume links with approval and visibility, readiness, per-feature consent.

epics.name: Phase 8 — Talent marketing
epics.goal: Assigned talent, job discovery and AI matching for a consultant, opportunity assignment and authorization, follow-ups, activities, duplicate guard — the marketer prepares, never submits.

epics.name: Phase 9 — Consultant applications, interviews, extension workspace
epics.goal: Consultant workspace, assigned jobs, application link via submit-detect, interview coordination, AI interview prep (licensed), offers, extension workspace selector.

epics.name: Phase 10 — Clients and placements
epics.goal: Client accounts, contacts, vendor relationships, requirements, candidate submissions (records), offers, placements, extensions and redeployment, Account Manager workspace.

epics.name: Phase 11 — HR and Finance
epics.goal: Lifecycle records, compliance checklists and policy acknowledgements without identity documents; finance records over the Timesheets product; reports.

epics.name: Phase 12 — Advanced analytics and enterprise features
epics.goal: Org analytics with k-anonymity, Autopilot prepare for assigned jobs, integrations, SSO, second-instance readiness, Cloudflare-for-SaaS evaluation.

stories.title: TenantResolver + TenantContext in the API, GET /api/public/tenant, internal tenant-hosts/check (ask) endpoint
stories.persona: Any visitor of a tenant host
stories.objective: The API decides the tenant from the host alone, never from a client-supplied id, and fails closed.
stories.story: As the API, I want to resolve X-Kiwiply-Host to exactly one tenant (or none) on every request so that every later check starts from a trustworthy tenant context.
stories.genz: The door knows whose house it is. You don't get to tell it.
functional: TenantResolverFilter (OncePerRequestFilter, before the JWT filter) reads X-Kiwiply-Host, normalises, resolves per 04 §2.2, stores TenantContext in a request attribute + ThreadLocal holder (cleared in finally) + MDC tenant/host.

Resolution cache: Caffeine, key host, TTL 60 s (setting enterprise.tenant.cache_seconds), evicted when organization.config_version changes (bumped by any hostname/branding/status write through OrgTenancyService). Negative cache: UNKNOWN results are cached 10 s (setting enterprise.tenant.negative_cache_seconds) and the cache is bounded at 10 000 entries (T13/T24 — enumeration bursts cannot evict live tenants or hammer the DB).
GET /api/public/tenant (permitAll, rate-limited per host+IP) returns PublicTenantDTO per 04 §2.4 for TENANT; 404 for UNKNOWN; for PLATFORM returns {kind:"PLATFORM"} only.

GET /api/internal/tenant-hosts/check?domain= (internal network) returns 200 for ACTIVE org_hostname rows of orgs ACTIVE/PAST_DUE and for {label}.kiwiply.com when subdomain_enabled; 404 otherwise; CUSTOM rows only when flag.enterprise.domains allows the org. Credential = a dedicated secret env DOSSIER_ASK_TOKEN (≠ DOSSIER_INTERNAL_TOKEN; 42 T17) accepted as X-Internal-Token on this endpoint or as query `t` (X3.3 adds the query form; constant-time compare; `t=` masked in access logs); the general internal token is NOT accepted here and the ask token is accepted nowhere else.
OrgPermissionInterceptor: if context is TENANT, path {orgId} must equal context.orgId else 404; if UNKNOWN, every /api/orgs/**, /api/me/orgs/**, /api/join/** → 404.
backend: config/TenantResolverFilter, service/ent/TenantResolver, service/ent/TenantContext(+Holder), web/rest/PublicTenantResource, web/rest/InternalTenantHostResource, OrgPermissionInterceptor change
db: None.
permissions: public; internal token

Host careers.acme.com with an ACTIVE row → TENANT; PENDING/VERIFIED/SUSPENDED/REMOVED → UNKNOWN; org SUSPENDED → UNKNOWN.

kiwiply.com, www., app., api., localhost → PLATFORM; nobody.example → UNKNOWN; missing header → UNKNOWN for tenant routes but PLATFORM-compatible for existing personal routes (no behaviour change for today's clients: the extension sends no header and keeps working).
A member of beta forging X-Kiwiply-Host: acme.kiwiply.com gets 200 on /api/public/tenant (public branding) and 404 on /api/orgs/{acme}/*.

stories.title: Web host resolution: proxy.ts carries the host and rewrites tenant hosts to /_t, serverApiFetch forwards X-Kiwiply-Host, getTenant(), (tenant)/%5Ft route group skeleton (URL /_t), tenant-404 page, tenant layout without Kiwiply chrome
stories.objective: The web app renders the tenant or a safe 404, never another tenant or the public site — without a second page at `/` (Next forbids two pages at one path, so tenant pages live under `(tenant)/_t/**` and proxy.ts rewrites to them).
stories.story: As a visitor on a tenant host, I want the site to know it is Acme's portal (or honestly say the workspace isn't available) so that I never land on the wrong company or the public marketing site.
stories.genz: Wrong address? You get a polite "not here", not someone else's lobby.
functional: web/src/proxy.ts: compute host (x-forwarded-host ?? host, lower-case, strip port); classify it PLATFORM (exact `localhost`, kiwiply.com, www/app/api/admin/edge.kiwiply.com, reserved list from 04 §2.2 — resolved FIRST) or candidate tenant; set internal request header x-kiwiply-host on every request; unchanged refresh logic (it now sends the host header too).

Rewrite (16 §2.3, escalation B2): for a non-platform host, `NextResponse.rewrite(new URL('/_t' + pathname + search, req.url))` for every path except `/api/*`, `/_next/*`, `/tenant-assets/*`, `/favicon.ico`, `/robots.txt` and files with an extension; a platform host requesting `/_t/*` directly is NOT rewritten and the (tenant) layout answers notFound(). The rewrite is applied before any host check so an UNKNOWN host still lands in the (tenant) layout (which renders the 404).
web/src/lib/api.ts serverApiFetch forwards X-Kiwiply-Host from the incoming request (headers()); tracker/resume proxies and the login/refresh route handlers inherit it.

web/src/lib/tenant.ts: getTenant() cached per request (React cache()) → {kind: PLATFORM|TENANT|UNKNOWN, tenant?: PublicTenantDTO}; PLATFORM for platform hosts without calling the API; when flag.enterprise is off (public-config orgs/enterprise flags) every non-platform host is UNKNOWN without calling the API; API 404 or failure → UNKNOWN (fail closed).

Route group web/src/app/(tenant)/%5Ft/ (Next.js treats a `_t` folder as private, so the directory on disk is the URL-encoded `%5Ft`; the public path stays `/_t`) with layout.tsx (the ONLY place the three kinds branch): UNKNOWN → render TenantUnavailable (HTTP 404, no branding, no links, no cookies, noindex); PLATFORM → notFound(); TENANT → sets <title> from tenant.displayName, lang/theme hooks for X2.12 (no theming yet) → children. No `(tenant)/page.tsx` at the root: `(marketing)/page.tsx` keeps `/`.

Skeleton pages under (tenant)/%5Ft/ in this story only: `_t/page.tsx` (TENANT: temporary "Portal coming soon" placeholder with the display name — X2.6 replaces it with the login-first redirect), `_t/login/page.tsx` placeholder (X2.3 replaces it with BrandedLogin), `_t/w/[workspace]/layout.tsx` placeholder that renders notFound() until X2.2. Every other path under _t/ falls through to Next's not-found inside the tenant layout (never the marketing 404).
Platform hosts keep today's (marketing)/(app)/(admin)/(org) behaviour untouched; `/org/*` on kiwiply.com stays the legacy console.
Dev: next dev accepts acme.localhost:3100 (`*.localhost` is tenant-only: `enterprise.hosts.tenant_base_domains`, only `localhost` itself is a platform host); mock-api resolves hosts (X1.12).

Root layout split: the Kiwiply chrome that `web/src/app/layout.tsx` mounts today (cookie-consent banner, bug-report widget, analytics/marketing scripts, SITE_URL metadata) moves into the platform route groups' layouts (`(marketing)`, `(app)`, `(admin)`, `(org)`) or a shared `PlatformChrome` component they each mount; the root layout keeps only `<html>/<body>`, fonts and theme providers. `(tenant)/%5Ft/layout.tsx` mounts none of it — no cookie banner, no bug-report, no third-party script, no Kiwiply links on tenant hosts (11 §7, 42 T19/T23).

proxy.ts matcher covers `/api/auth/*` and every BFF route (`/api/*` route handlers are not rewritten, but the matcher must still run so `x-kiwiply-host` is set on them); the matcher table is unit-tested. The BFF (`serverApiFetch`, the auth route handlers) never forwards `X-Forwarded-Host` upstream — only `X-Kiwiply-Host` (42 T23, X1.13 `PublicHostGuardFilter`); the host is taken from `X-Forwarded-Host` only because the shared edge overwrites it (44 §6.2 spoof test), never from a client-settable header on a platform host.

stories.title: Tenant-bound sessions: tid/hid claims on tenant-host login, decoder validation, refresh keeps tid, interceptor enforces tid = path org
stories.persona: Acme employee signing in on careers.acme.com
stories.objective: A session from one tenant is useless on another, even if a token leaks.
stories.story: As a security architect, I want tokens minted on a tenant host to be bound to that tenant so that replaying them against another tenant or the platform org console fails.
stories.genz: Your badge opens your building. Not the one next door.
functional: POST /api/authenticate (+/mfa, /auth/google, /refresh) on a TENANT context adds claims tid=<orgId>, hid=<hostnameId> to both tokens; requires the user to be an ACTIVE, non-reserved member of that org — otherwise 403 NOT_A_MEMBER (the only non-404 here, the login page needs it) with no org data.

JwtDecoder validator: tid present and context TENANT → tid must equal context.orgId (else 401 TOKEN_TENANT_MISMATCH); tid present and context PLATFORM → token accepted for user-scoped routes only, 404 on /api/orgs/{any}; tid absent and context TENANT → unauthenticated on tenant routes except /api/account (login-first hand-off).
Refresh rotation preserves tid/hid; /api/logout unchanged; /api/extension/session never adds tid.
Web login route handlers forward X-Kiwiply-Host (already by X1.4); cookies unchanged (host-only).

OriginCheckFilter (42 T27): every non-GET/HEAD request authenticated by cookie must carry an Origin (else Referer) whose host equals the resolved tenant host or one of the org's other ACTIVE hostnames; missing both ⇒ generic 404 (WARN logged); Bearer-token (extension) requests are exempt; the BFF applies the same check. Cookies on tenant hosts use the `__Host-` prefix (Secure, Path=/, no Domain; 42 T19) — `dossier.cookies.host-prefix` default true, false allowed only in the mock/dev profile (ProdConfigIT asserts).

proxy.ts/BFF: the /api/auth/* route handlers forward X-Kiwiply-Host on every call (login, mfa, google, refresh, logout) — the proxy matcher includes them (X1.4); a tenant-host refresh whose cookie tid ≠ resolved tenant is refused and the BFF clears the cookies (STALE_SESSION in X2.3).
ui: Login page on tenant hosts (unbranded placeholder until X2.3): NOT_A_MEMBER renders "You're not a member of this workspace" with no data and a sign-out link.
backend: AuthenticateController, GoogleAuthController, SecurityJwtConfiguration validator, SecurityUtils (TENANT_CLAIM = "tid"), OrgPermissionInterceptor
db: None.
apis: Existing auth endpoints; new 403 NOT_A_MEMBER on tenant hosts
permissions: membership ACTIVE
ac: Token minted on acme host decodes with tid=acme; used on beta host → 401; used on kiwiply.com /api/orgs/{acme} → 404; used on kiwiply.com /api/account → 200.
Personal token (no tid) on acme host → GET /api/orgs/{acme}/… 401 (not 404) so the web redirects to the tenant login; GET /api/account → 200.
Refresh on acme host returns tokens with the same tid; the old family revocation still applies.
Extension tokens carry no tid before and after.
Non-member login on acme host → 403 NOT_A_MEMBER, no Set-Cookie, audit row LOGIN_DENIED_NOT_MEMBER in acme's org_audit_event with hostname_id.

POST /api/orgs/{acme}/… from evil.kiwiply.com with acme cookies (Origin: https://evil.kiwiply.com) → 404 and nothing changes; same request with Origin: https://acme.kiwiply.com → normal; a request with neither Origin nor Referer → 404; an extension Bearer request without Origin → normal (OriginCheckFilterIT, SEC-16).
Cookies set on acme.localhost are named with the __Host- prefix and carry Secure + Path=/ and no Domain attribute (cookie assertion in AuthenticateControllerIT and Playwright).
POST /api/auth/refresh on acme.localhost with a beta-minted refresh cookie → 401 and Set-Cookie clearing both cookies (AuthRouteForwardsHostTest).
tests: Web auth route tests forward the host.

/management/info → ROLE_ADMIN. /management/health and /management/health/{liveness,readiness} stay permitAll with management.endpoint.health.show-details=never (monitors keep working; DEPLOY.md expectation {"status":"UP"} unchanged).

PublicHostGuardFilter (OncePerRequestFilter, @Order(HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE + 5), ahead of both security chains) answers 404 (empty body, same as an unknown route, before any token check) for any request to /api/internal/** or /management/** (except the health paths) when either (a) it carries X-Forwarded-Host (the edge always sets it; compose-internal callers — web BFF, Caddy's ask call, Docker healthchecks — never do), or (b) its Host (port stripped) is not in the internal allow-list setting enterprise.hosts.internal (HIGH, EnterpriseSettingKeys.Ops, default ["localhost","127.0.0.1","[::1]","api","dossier-api","web","dossier-web"]) — fail-closed. Master switch dossier.internal.refuse-public-host (default true; tests set it per case).
The BFF (serverApiFetch) must not forward X-Forwarded-Host to the API (X1.4 AC; the host travels only as X-Kiwiply-Host) — BffDoesNotForwardForwardedHostTest.

stories.title: Second-instance readiness: ShedLock on every @Scheduled job, DB-backed shared rate limiters and counters, cross-instance cache invalidation (config_version polling + cache_invalidation table), stateless-session audit, compose `--scale api=2` rehearsal and runbook
stories.story: As the operator, I want to scale the API to two instances when load requires it, knowing jobs run once and caches stay coherent.
stories.genz: Two engines, one brain.
ac: Two app contexts against one DB: a job scheduled every 10 s runs exactly once per tick across both (ShedLock IT); SchedulerLockedTest fails on a new @Scheduled method without @SchedulerLock.
Rate-limit of 5/min reached on instance A is enforced on instance B within the same window (DbRateLimiterIT).
A config_version bump on A evicts B's resolver entry within 5 s (CacheInvalidationIT); tenant resolution stays ≤ 50 ms p95 from cache.
No in-memory login/MFA state remains (grep-style ArchUnit rule over a deny-list of ConcurrentHashMap singletons in security packages).
stories.tech: Fully specified by Session E. ADR-022; 44 §9.2 trigger "a second API instance only after X12.5"; no Redis (box memory). Jobs added by earlier phases already say "ShedLock-ready" — this story turns it on.
db: Liquibase 20261026070000_ent_ops.xml: shedlock, rate_limit_bucket, cache_invalidation (platform tables).
stories.persona: Platform operator; every job and limiter in the codebase
stories.objective: A second API container can be started without double-running a job, double-counting a limit or serving a stale tenant from cache (ADR-022: design for two, run one).
functional: ShedLock (JDBC provider, table shedlock in 20261026070000_ent_ops.xml) on every @Scheduled job (an ArchUnit test fails on an unlocked scheduler); lock names = job class; lockAtMostFor per job (≤ the schedule interval).

Rate limiters (JoinRateLimiter, tenant public endpoints, ask endpoint, login) move from in-memory to a DB-backed sliding window (rate_limit_bucket (key, window_start, count)) with a Caffeine front cache; semantics unchanged (table-driven tests); per-org caps of 42 T65 use the same store.

Cache invalidation: resolver/membership/catalog caches keyed by config_version/catalog_version already evict on change within one instance; add cache_invalidation (id, scope, key, at) rows written on every bump and a 5-s poller per instance that evicts matching entries (no Redis on the box); verified by a two-instance IT (Testcontainers: two app contexts, one DB).

Sessions are stateless JWT (04 §3) — audit any remaining in-memory state (MFA challenges → DB rows (X2.14 note), admin_mfa_challenge, quote drafts) and move it to the DB; compose rehearsal doc: `docker compose … up -d --scale api=2` behind the shared edge with health-based routing (44 §9.2) — operator-run, documented in DEPLOY.md.
permissions: None.

stories.genz: Tap your key, you're in.
stories.title: TOTP and passkeys (WebAuthn) as second factors for every user; org.security.mfa_method (EMAIL|TOTP|PASSKEY|ANY) lets an org require a stronger factor than the emailed code; recovery codes; /me → Security enrolment; admin reset with reason
stories.persona: Every member (enrolment); Org Admin setting the policy
stories.objective: Orgs that cannot accept email codes can require an authenticator app or a passkey, and nobody is locked out without a recovery path.
stories.story: As an org admin, I want to require an authenticator or passkey for everyone at Acme so that a mailbox compromise is not an account compromise.
functional: user_mfa_method (login, kind TOTP|PASSKEY, secret/credential (SecretBox / WebAuthn credential id + public key), label, created_at, last_used_at) and user_recovery_code (hashed, single-use, 10 per set); enrolment flows on /me → Security (13): TOTP (QR + verify), passkey (WebAuthn registration, platform or roaming), recovery codes download-once; remove with re-auth.

LoginMfaService (X2.14) generalised: challenge kind chosen by org.security.mfa_method — EMAIL (today), TOTP, PASSKEY or ANY (user picks among enrolled methods); when the org requires a method the member lacks → post-login enrolment gate (cannot enter a workspace until enrolled; grace enterprise.mfa.enrol_grace_days, default 7, shown as a banner); platform admins unaffected (existing AdminMfaService stays email + may add TOTP).
Admin reset: ORG_ADMIN may reset a member's second factor (ReasonSheet HIGH, notification to the member, audit MFA_RESET) — never view secrets; platform admin same for admins.
backend: security/mfa/{TotpService, WebAuthnService (webauthn4j or Spring Security WebAuthn), RecoveryCodeService}; LoginMfaService (extend); web/rest/MeMfaResource; OrgSettings key org.security.mfa_method
apis: GET/POST/DELETE /api/me/mfa/methods[/{id}] · POST /api/me/mfa/totp/verify · POST /api/me/mfa/webauthn/options | /register · POST /api/me/mfa/recovery-codes · POST /api/authenticate/mfa (extended: {code | assertion | recoveryCode}) · POST /api/orgs/{orgId}/members/{id}/mfa/reset {reason}
permissions: self for enrolment; members.security.reset (ORG_ADMIN) for reset; org.settings.manage for the policy
ac: With org.security.mfa_method=TOTP, a member without TOTP sees the enrolment gate after password login and cannot open /w/* until enrolled (grace banner when within grace); after enrolment the login completes with the TOTP code; an email code is refused.
Passkey registration + assertion succeed on the tenant host origin (rpId = host) and fail from another origin; recovery code works once and is then invalid.
Admin reset removes the methods, notifies the member and writes MFA_RESET HIGH; the admin never sees a secret.
Platform-host (kiwiply.com) personal logins behave exactly as before unless the user enrolled voluntarily (regression suite).
stories.tech: Split from X12.4 by Session E (11 §3.4 note: TOTP/passkeys ride with the SSO phase). Dependency review for the WebAuthn lib (42 T64). rpId = the tenant host, so passkeys are per host by design (12 §9: no central SSO).
stories.dod: Stronger factors available; org policy enforceable; tracker Completed. Plus the common DoD in `06-phase-plan.md` §5.
